Simulate TITE-gBOIN-ET Trials

Source: R/tite_gboin_et_simulate.R
tite_gboin_et_simulate.Rd

Run the TITE-gBOIN-ET dose-finding algorithm of Takeda, Yamaguchi, Taguri and Morita (2023) over many simulated trials, for toxicity and efficacy outcomes with several categories that each carry a score, in which patients arrive over time and the outcomes are assessed over windows, and return the patients, their categories and the total scores at every dose. This is the simulation engine behind sim_tite_gboin_et, exposed for users who want the raw trial data.

Usage

tite_gboin_et_simulate(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_grade,
  p_resp_grade,
  score,
  score_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  window,
  accrual_rate,
  resp_window = window,
  accrual = c("uniform", "exponential", "fixed"),
  event_time = c("weibull", "uniform"),
  late_fraction = 0.5,
  resp_late_fraction = 0.5,
  resp_cor = 0.2,
  min_completed_share = 0.5,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  lambda1 = NULL,
  lambda2 = NULL,
  eta1 = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  boinet_compatible = FALSE,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized toxicity score, for example 0.47 / 1.5 for a target equivalent toxicity score of 0.47 with a largest score of 1.5.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized efficacy score, for example 0.95 / 1.5 for a target equivalent efficacy score of 0.95 with a largest score of 1.5.

p_grade

Numeric matrix. True probability of each toxicity category (rows) at each dose (columns, in increasing dose order). Every column sums to 1. The first row is the category without a toxicity event.

p_resp_grade

Numeric matrix with one column per dose. True probability of each efficacy category (rows). Every column sums to 1. The first row is the category without an efficacy event.

score

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_grade. Score of each toxicity category, for example c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5) for grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4. The scores are divided by their maximum.

score_resp

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_resp_grade. Score of each efficacy category, for example c(0, 1, 1.5) for stable or progressive disease, partial response and complete response. The scores are divided by their maximum.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

window

Numeric scalar. Length of the toxicity assessment window.

accrual_rate

Numeric scalar. Average number of patients arriving per unit of time, in the same unit as window. The accrual argument of the 'boinet' package is the average time between arrivals, its inverse.

resp_window

Numeric scalar. Length of the efficacy assessment window. Defaults to window.

accrual

Character scalar. Distribution of the times between arrivals: "uniform" (the default, as in 'boinet') on (0, 2 / accrual_rate), "exponential" for a Poisson process, or "fixed" for arrivals exactly 1 / accrual_rate apart.

event_time

Character scalar. Distribution of the times to the toxicity event and to the efficacy event: "weibull" (the default), with the share of the events in the second half of the window set by late_fraction and resp_late_fraction, or "uniform" on (0, window / p) for an event of probability p. With "weibull" the first category of both outcomes, the one without an event, must have a positive probability at every dose.

late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. Share of the toxicity events that occur in the second half of the toxicity window under the Weibull distribution. Defaults to 0.5.

resp_late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. The same for the efficacy events. Defaults to 0.5.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar strictly between -1 and 1. Correlation of the Gaussian copula that links the time to the toxicity event and the time to the efficacy event of a patient. Defaults to 0.2, the default of the 'boinet' package.

min_completed_share

Numeric scalar from 0 to 1. Share of the patients at the current dose who must have finished both assessments before the next decision; the decision waits until then. Defaults to 0.5, the rule of Takeda et al. (2023) and of the 'boinet' package.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at any dose. Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size, which is the default of the 'boinet' package.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

Numeric scalars or NULL. Boundaries of the mean toxicity score and of the mean efficacy score. Defaults to NULL, the boundaries of boin_et_boundary for the targets. Give all three to use other values, such as those printed in an article.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

boinet_compatible

Logical scalar. Apply the rules of the 'boinet' package (version 1.6.0) exactly. Defaults to FALSE, which keeps to Takeda et al. (2018), who do not allow dose skipping during escalation; see Details.

prior

Numeric vector of length 6. Prior probabilities of the six hypotheses. Defaults to rep(1 / 6, 6), the noninformative choice of the article. The third hypothesis, under which every decision is correct, does not enter the criterion.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin_et_trials, as returned by gboin_et_simulate, with design set to "TITE-gBOIN-ET" and one more component

duration

Numeric vector of the time of the last decision of each trial, which is the trial duration when all cohorts are enrolled.

The categories and the total scores are those observed at the last decision; a patient still under assessment is counted in the first category.

Details

The TITE-gBOIN-ET design is the gBOIN-ET design (gboin_et_simulate) for outcomes that are observed late: the next cohort is enrolled while earlier patients are still assessed. The first patient of a cohort arrives at the time of the previous decision, and the next decision is due when the next patient arrives; after the last cohort it is due once every patient has been followed over both windows. While fewer than a share min_completed_share of the patients at the current dose have finished both assessments, the decision waits for the next assessment to end.

At a decision, the mean toxicity score of a dose is the total of the normalized scores observed so far divided by the effective number of patients: the patients whose toxicity assessment has ended plus, for every patient still under assessment, the fraction of the window followed so far (Takeda et al., 2023). The mean efficacy score is formed in the same way, and the decision rule of gBOIN-ET is applied to the two means of the current dose. The admissibility of a dose uses the total scores observed so far and the number of patients treated at the dose, so that a patient still under assessment counts as a patient without an event, and the moves between doses follow boin_et_simulate, including the changes from 'boinet' unless boinet_compatible is TRUE. These are the rules of boinet::tite.gboinet().

A patient has a toxicity event when the time to the event falls within the window, which happens with the probability of the categories above the first, and an efficacy event likewise. The two event times come from their marginal distributions linked by a Gaussian copula, and the category of a patient with an event is drawn from the probabilities of the categories above the first, independently of everything else; it is observed at the time of the event, and a patient without an event is known to have none when the window ends. Each patient draws one uniform variate for the toxicity event, one for the efficacy event, and one more for each outcome with more than two categories. With two categories of scores 0 and 1 for both outcomes the trials are, for the same seed, those of tite_boin_et_simulate; with arrivals a fixed time apart that is longer than both windows, they are those of gboin_et_simulate. The 'boinet' package draws its random numbers differently, so the trials agree with it in distribution, not one by one.

The program of the supporting information of Takeda et al. (2023) differs from these rules in two points. Where one dose among the current dose and its neighbors has the highest mean efficacy score, the program passes that dose to sample(), which then draws from all doses up to it, so that the trial can move to any lower dose; and the program excludes doses with the effective numbers of patients in the place of the numbers of patients. Neither is described in the article, and 'boinet' has neither. The first changes the published operating characteristics substantially; see inst/reproduce/reproduce_Takeda2023.R.

The mean score of a dose is computed as the total of the scores as given, divided by the largest score times the effective number of patients, as in gboin_et_simulate; when no patient of the dose is still under assessment, doses whose mean scores are equal as fractions tie on every platform.

Possible values of stop_reason are those of boin_et_simulate.

References

Takeda, K., Yamaguchi, Y., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2023). TITE-gBOIN-ET: Time-to-event generalized Bayesian optimal interval design to accelerate dose-finding accounting for ordinal graded efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Biometrical Journal, 65(7), 2200265. doi:10.1002/bimj.202200265

Yamaguchi, Y., Takeda, K. and Maruo, K. (2025). boinet: An R Package for Bayesian Optimal Interval Design for Dose Finding Based on Both Efficacy and Toxicity Outcomes. The R Journal, 17(2), 15-34. doi:10.32614/RJ-2025-012

See also

sim_tite_gboin_et, gboin_et_select_obd, gboin_et_simulate, tite_boin_et_simulate

Examples

# Toxicity grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4, and progressive disease, stable
# disease, partial response and complete response, at four doses, with a
# 30-day toxicity window, a 60-day efficacy window and one patient every
# 10 days on average
p_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.94, 0.79, 0.62, 0.50),
  c(0.05, 0.15, 0.20, 0.20),
  c(0.01, 0.05, 0.15, 0.25),
  c(0.00, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05)
)
p_resp_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.64, 0.45, 0.20, 0.05),
  c(0.30, 0.40, 0.40, 0.15),
  c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35),
  c(0.01, 0.05, 0.20, 0.45)
)
trials <- tite_gboin_et_simulate(
  target = 0.47 / 1.5, target_resp = 1.75 / 3,
  p_grade = p_grade, p_resp_grade = p_resp_grade,
  score = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5), score_resp = c(0, 0.25, 1, 3),
  n_cohort = 12, cohort_size = 3, window = 30, resp_window = 60,
  accrual_rate = 1 / 10, n_trials = 200, seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated TITE-gBOIN-ET trials
#>   trials               : 200
#>   doses                : 4
#>   target toxicity score: 0.3133333
#>   target efficacy score: 0.5833333
#>   cohorts              : 12 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 36
#> 
#> Average per trial:
#>                   DL1  DL2   DL3   DL4
#> Patients treated 3.15 4.16 10.05 18.64
#> Toxicity score   0.07 0.39  1.94  5.56
#> Efficacy score   0.16 0.53  3.06 10.77
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#> max_cohorts 
#>         100 
#> 
#> Average trial duration: 499.9
summary(trials$duration)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   405.0   476.0   502.4   499.9   525.8   596.3
